input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
input.rationale: Section 22.1 grants Vendor unlimited, unannounced audits of Customer plus remote access to our systems — squarely in the playbook walk-away zone. The rule requires no more than one audit per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and no direct access to Customer systems. Sections 22.2 (Vendor cost unless >5% underpayment; no direct system access) and 22.3 (findings confidential) already meet the playbook, and Section 23 contains no additional records-inspection rights, so the minimal fix is to rewrite 22.1 with the frequency, notice, scope and access limits.

ops.oldText: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
ops.newText: Vendor may audit Customer's use of the Services no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during Customer's normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer's operations. The audit shall be conducted by an independent auditor that is not a Customer competitor and that is bound by written confidentiality obligations at least as protective as Section 16. The audit shall be limited to a review of records relevant to Customer's use of the Services, conducted remotely from the auditor's own facilities or at a mutually agreed location, and Vendor and its auditor shall have no direct or remote access to Customer's systems.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have limited audits to once per twelve months on thirty days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and removed the right of remote access to our systems, consistent with our playbook position that audits be rare, notified and off-site (records review only). Cost allocation in Section 22.2 is acceptable as drafted; if helpful we can accept fifteen days' notice as a fallback.
proposal.summary: Limit Vendor audit right to once per 12 months on 30 days' notice, business hours, independent confidential auditor, records-only with no system access.
